Sophie Bretag mentioned your company in an update
I realised why I’ve taken nearly eight weeks to share this... It’s because I haven’t really had the right words for it until now. 🌻 My lovely Dad, ever the wordsmith, explained it beautifully to me the other day “...the vast room seemed to shrink because we were surrounded by so much warmth and love.” 📙 When I think back to launching my book, The Kind Way, at Dymocks Adelaide at the end of July, what comes back to me isn’t really the fact that we oversold tickets or that the room was overflowing with people. It’s how the room felt. 🧡 There were smiles, hugs and laughter and everywhere I looked was another human who has meant something to me along the way. My family is small, but having them all there meant the absolute world to me, alongside friends, clients, colleagues and beautiful humans who have come into my life through so many different ways. 🎤 My fabulous host (and friend!) Tamsin Simounds held the conversation with so much warmth and kindness that I could simply share the stories behind the work. My beautiful best friend Rebecca Keevers stood up and spoke words I’ll treasure for a very long time, and then my 2 boys stood in front of everyone and talked about what it meant to them to have their mama as a published author. 🤩 I will never forget how proud I felt of them being so brave. 🩷 Even the little details that I organised were an extension of what my book is about, with 1000 Hearts and Jurlique (thank you Sarah De Jonge and Cherie Hutchinson) generously partnering with me to create gifts for everyone who came, adding even more care and kindness to a room already full of it. 🙏 I wrote a book about kindness, about being human, about protecting our capacity and remembering that we matter too, and for one beautiful night I got to feel all of that reflected back at me through the people who showed up. 🙌 I’m incredibly proud of this book and everything it has gone on to do in the short 10 weeks it’s been published (hello 3 print runs and a billboard in Times Square...!), but when I think about my book journey, the numbers aren’t what I’ll remember. 🤗 I’ll remember the smiling faces, my best friend speaking, my boys standing there so bravely. The hugs, the laughter and the warmth that somehow filled every corner of that very big room. 💖 Mostly, I’ll remember what it felt like to be surrounded by people who genuinely wanted to be there, celebrating something that means so very much to me. I’ll never stop being grateful for that. 🥰 To everyone who came to my launch in Adelaide, thankyou! To those of you who sent your well wishes, thankyou! To everyone who has bought, referred or reviewed my book, thankyou! I know that this is just the beginning. Kindest Soph 🌈☀️ (SO many beautiful pics of beautiful humans - this gives you the vibe I hope of what the night created for us all). Kelly Irving Expert Author Community Natasha Gilmour Dymocks Adelaide

Danielle Duell mentioned your company in a comment
Expert Author Community - Thank you. ⭐ I've learned so much and met so many amazing humans+authors since being part of this community. It's had a big influence on how I've approached the whole book. 
It’s official: I just signed with Grammar Factory to publish my book! This year, I'm writing the guide leaders have been asking for: how to put purpose into practice, not leave it as words on a wall. Choosing a publisher was a decision I didn't take lightly and I was fortunate to have a choice. That's not something every author gets and I didn't want to waste it. I kept coming back to the question: who could help us get this book into the hands of leaders globally, while staying true to our purpose 'to equip business to improve the world,' and creating a sustainable path for our business? Grammar Factory was the answer. I first connected through Kelly Irving's Expert Author Community, and from my first conversation with Scott A. MacMillan, I had a strong sense we’d found the right partner. Scott patiently answered a lot of questions and gave me the confidence that the ideas I’ve been carrying for years were in good hands. My team and I at People With Purpose* are incredibly excited to be working with the Grammar Factory team to bring the book to life, and ultimately to help leaders close the gap between purpose intent and purpose in practice. More to come soon.

Chloe Cooper mentioned your company in an update
Not going to lie, I lost hope this day would ever happen. In 2021, I announced here on LI that I was writing a book. 5 years have gone by, and every "how's the book going?" since has landed like a small personal failure. I was stuck in a shame spiral... ...because I just couldn’t do it. I literally, no matter how hard I tried, could not get this damn thing over the line. Despite surrounding myself with amazing communities like Kelly Irving Expert Author Community and befriending countless authors. Big shout-out to my podmates Siobhán O'Riordan TyAnn Osborn Monique Zytnik Jennifer Doyle Vancil, M.Ed., PCC I sat back watching others lead the way, heart aching that for whatever reason, I couldn’t get myself to do the same. Ryan Hopkins - remember sharing with you blooming years back and I think you're now on round 2. Well, it’s finally happening. I’m doing this a bit backwards, because whilst you can see the printed version here, it’s still a WIP. But here’s the thing: for the next 12 weeks, I’m going to take you behind the scenes of getting this into the world. It's called The Fulfilment Habit. It’ll be out in December.  And for the next twelve weeks, I'm going to show the whole shabangle. Every bit it takes to self-publish a book INCLUDING the money bits, the costs involved and the big fat hairy £80k goal I’m aiming for. And so, if you are one of the hundreds of people who've asked me about the book at any point in the last five years: thank you for your patience, and sorry it’s taken so long, but here it is. P.S. I’ve recorded myself reading the first two parts. It’s totally free to listen to; just check out the comments on the link.

Anna Featherstone mentioned your company in an update
Some books can't be squeezed onto a standard publishing shelf. Especially when they're a mix of magical realism, mind and art. So what do you do when you have a very specific vision and handing over creative control doesn't feel right? Clinical psychologist Bee Lim, Ph.D. answered that question with custom publishing, and she shares her reasoning in my latest conversation for the Self-Publishing with Alliance of Independent Authors (ALLi) Podcast (link in comments). Her book, 'Welcome Home: Healing Trauma & Reclaiming Wholeness', is an illustrated narrative non-fiction hardcover, a reflective story rather than a self-help manual, born from noticing her clients connected with mental health concepts better through narrative and metaphor than clinical explanation. Amongst other things we talk about: → Custom publishing: keeping IP and creative control while relying on an established publisher's production and distribution experience → Endorsements: the email Bee almost didn't send to an Ivy League professor, and the connection it sparked → Writing and marketing as a regulated health professional: unsolicited reviews only, client confidentiality first, and positioning the book as a resource, never a treatment → Translation rights: Chinese rights being pitched currently, another area where indie authors have agency I first met Bee at Kelly Irving's Expert Author Community on the fabulous pitch day, where authors pitch their concepts to publishers and industry professionals. Watching Bee take that concept all the way to a beautifully produced book has been a privilege. It's great timing too because if you're a health and medical professional, I'm co-hosting a live workshop with healthcare thought leadership strategist Megan Walker on Friday 11 September, ‘How to Write and Publish a HealthCare Book’. If that's of interest, see you there. Links in the comments.

Jennifer Doyle Vancil, M.Ed., PCC mentioned your company in an update
I'd love to recommend my friend Siobhán O'Riordan's book "Reframe" for anyone who identifies as a "generalist" rather than a specialist. Fans of our "strengths-based career" philosophy will find Siobhan's book challenging you to get clear on your strengths and learn to communicate them as part of the way you can find your next opportunities. Even if you aren't a specialist "accountant" or "marketing director" or some other specific title. Many of the career explorers I work with might identify as generalists and I'm so excited to have Siobhan's book to support our work. I had the honor of partnering with Siobhan in a writing group when we were both in the Expert Author Community so I've watched this book develop and now that it's out, I've now sent her book to my clients and I've read it myself and I can say wholeheartedly, it's worth our time.
